newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods--Group gasoline only game in town.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods--Group gasoline only game in town.

text.p: Gasoline markets in Group Three showed the only signs of life if cash refined petroleum markets east of the Rocky Mountains on Thursday morning on continued views supplies were tight in the region.

Action in New York Harbor and at the U.S. Gulf Coast were meanwhile rather subdued due to a number of industry functions this week that have pulled players away from trading desks and onto into meeting rooms and golf courses for business and fun.
"The only action I've seen is the differentials in Group Three for gasoline which continue to roar," said one trader, noting USG and NYH markets were steady if not inexistent.
- MIDCONTINENT

++ Gasoline: In Group Three, any-month gasoline differentials took center stage amid spirited buying that pushed differentials up a cent from Wednesday's levels to 5.00 cents over June futures, traders said.
Traders said scheduling requirements were being stirred into a bullish mix of delays on the Explorer Pipeline amid continued low inventories in the Midcontinent region.

"There's a lot of short covering because of the Explorer Pipeline delays," the trader said, noting the pipeline is running five to ten days behind schedule on deliveries and is not expected to deliver 14th cycle gasoline from the Gulf to Tulsa until early June.
"A lot of people had sold any-month barrels but it looks like they won't get here in time, so they have to cover their commitments," the trader said.

Dead prompt Group Three unleaded differentials meanwhile remained at Wednesday's firm levels of 7.25 cents over June NYMEX. Slightly deferred barrels were heard talked at between 5.50 and 5.75 cents over June NYMEX, while any month barrels were talked widely between 4.00 and 5.00 cents over.
The Explorer delays were originally caused by maintenance done by Explorer in April, industry sources said.
Prompt Chicago conventional unleaded, meanwhile, was little changed at between 2.50 and 2.75 cents over the print while any-month barrels eased about 0.25 cent to 2.00 cents over, players said.

++ Distillates: The Explorer delays also kept upward pressure on Group low sulphur diffs, which also remained at firmer levels first heard Wednesday between 6.75 cents and 7.00 cents over the June screen.
- NEW YORK HARBOR
Talk in NYH was effectively doused by the "New York Harbor Supply Conference" being held just to the north of New York City, since it pulled so many traders out of action.

That event came on the heels of NYMEX's unveiling Wednesday evening of its new trading floor on the edge of the Hudson River in New York's financial district -- an event attended by as many as 1,500 industry participants.

++ GASOLINE: Differentials remained notionally pegged at Wednesday's levels, with "A2" regular reformulated gasoline still offered at 1.25 cents over June NYMEX unleaded, and "M2" regular conventional talked at between 1.85 and 1.60 cents under the June print.
- U.S. GULF
Gulf trade was also hurt by the industry events in the New York area, which included a bowling outing on Wednesday evening ahead of the Supply Conference, traders said.

++ GASOLINE: Traders said regular "M1" conventional gasoline was talked at between 4.00 and 3.75 cents under June NYMEX, with regular reformulated "A1" still talked at between 1.00 and 0.75 cent below the June print.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633
